To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the E2 recombinant antigen was able to detect antibodies in 88% of RIBA‐2 indeterminate HCV‐RNA‐positive samples.

the E2 recombinant antigen was able to resolve most of the Riba‐2‐indeterminate samples, and that NS5 and E 2 antibodies did not emerge earlier than the classical HCV antibodies in serial samples from nine patients with post‐transfusion hepatitis C.

E2 and NS5 antibodies were present in 88% and 36% respectively of HCV‐RNA‐positive, Riba‐indeterminate sera, but in only 13% of HCV‐negative Riba‐indetermi nates; and that E2 antibodies appeared in all posttransfusion HCV cases, whereas NS5 antibodies did not.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the interaction of a protein, the enzyme superoxide dismutase (SOD), with a small molecule, the superoxide ion.
the development of a new method for the detection of hepatitis C viruses (HCVs) in blood.
the development of new diagnostic methods for the detection of HCV.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
E2 and NS5 antigens are useful for the diagnosis of HCV infection.
the recombinant E‐2 and NS‐5 antigens can be used for the diagnosis of HCV infection.
the E2 antigen is a good candidate antigen for the development of a future hepatitis C virus antibody assay.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
E2 is a good candidate for a future HCV assay.
E2 and NS5 are new antigens for detection HCV antibodies.
E2 antigen is more sensitive and more specific than NS5 antigen.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of the recombinant E1 and E2 antigens in a screening assay for HCV infection is not likely to improve the sensitivity of the assay over current screening assays that use the recombinant core antigen.
the E2 antigen is more sensitive than the recombinant NS5 antigen for detecting HCV antibodies, and the recombinant E antigen is the most sensitive antigen for detecting HVC antibodies.
the E2 and NS5 antigens are not useful for early detection of hepatitis C infection.
